intended_object: The rational number 1 in the ZFC model of ℚ, built as the quotient of ℤ × ℤ∖{0} by (a,b) ~ (c,d) ⇔ ad = bc. It is the class of the fraction 1/1. Inferred from the name, the file's module doc, and its use as the `One ZFRat` instance.
explanation: `ZFRat` is the quotient of `ZFInt × ZFInt'` (pairs made of an integer and a nonzero integer) by the usual fraction relation. `one` is the class of (1, 1), the standard representative of 1/1. In turn, `ZFInt.one` is `mk (1, 0)`, the class of 1 − 0 in the usual construction of ℤ, so it really is the integer 1. The definition is a specific constant inside this library's own ZFC-based construction, so the question of generality does not come up. Mathlib's `(1 : ℚ)` lives in a different model of ℚ and is not the same declaration, so there is no Mathlib counterpart to cite.
